body:
MAINLINE-072b is filed. No real core makes the graphite route feasible. QUESTIONABLE. PROJECTION. No qualified hull safety factor.

Cores at or below 12.2e-6 per K exist in four families, all datasheet-typical. Kevlar publishes 4.86e-6/K (HRH-49 1/4-2.1, full data, flagged preliminary). Carbon publishes 4.5e-6/K across thickness (UCF-51; UCF-355 carries the family value with full data). Glass publishes 14.76e-6/K. Titanium, beryllium and Invar are braze-formed demonstrations, not catalog cores.

071's model copy, reproductions 0.0 and 0.001 kg; gamma by the CR-1457 step; the film keeps -1.0e-6/K.

Carbon UCF-355: no feasible geometry in any of the 8 cases. The low expansion is real, but the core's own bond-shear stiffness (3.3x CR-III) holds the interface under the 25 psi screen. Release needs alpha at or below 3.0e-6, or a wall modulus under about 18 GPa - a value the maker does not publish.

Glass HRH-327: no feasible geometry; release needs 8.8e-6, under every published glass value.

Kevlar HRH-49: feasible in all 8 cases - the first core whose published expansion the film carries (interface 3.86). The cost is mechanical: W shear modulus 0.19 of CR-III drives the core to 108-166 mm and scarf shear and crimping bind. Payloads -27250 to -97399 kg. The face-density factor to float is 2.67-3.04 at concept (to 741-842 kg/m3) and 2.16-2.41 at TRL 7 (934-1042), against CR-III's gamma-step 1.07-1.25.

The route's named needs: the carbon grades' wall modulus and in-plane CTE measured; a stiffer Kevlar-family core at that expansion; and the face itself.
